channel.title: Did you know? | Dark Side Energy
channel.description: Articles by Dark Side Energy on event power distribution: key notions, methods and field know-how.

item.title: Why do LEDs trip RCDs?
item.description: Leakage and inrush currents: why LEDs and electronics trip 30 mA RCDs, and how to split circuits to avoid it.

item.title: Single-phase or three-phase: why balance the phases?
item.description: Single-phase 230 V, three-phase 400 V: why spread loads over L1, L2 and L3, and how the most loaded phase sets the size of the source.

item.title: What is the diversity factor?
item.description: The diversity factor explained simply: not all equipment runs at full power at the same time. How to apply it in a power assessment.

item.title: kVA or kW: what's the difference?
item.description: kW and kVA explained simply: active power, apparent power and cos φ. Why generators and grid connections are rated in kVA.

item.title: How much power can you draw from a P17 socket?
item.description: How many kVA behind a P17 socket? Reference figures from 16 A to 125 A and for a 400 A Powerlock, the margin to keep and why cable length matters.

item.title: Cable size depends on current, but also on length!
item.description: Why cable size depends on current but also on length: resistance, heating and voltage drop, explained simply.

item.title: What is event power distribution?
item.description: Event power distribution: starting from the venue's supplies to distribute electricity safely. And why taking power from the next stand is banned.

item.title: What is a Twin zero-interruption generator set?
item.description: Twin zero-interruption generator set: two synchronised generators, each carrying 50% of the load. If one fails, there is no interruption.

item.title: Why does it “trip”?
item.description: Why a distribution box “trips”: 30 mA RCD and circuit breaker explained simply. Faulty appliance or overloaded circuit?
